correctness.rationale: For every vertex-deletion-connected finite simple base G of order >=3, the all-leaf simplex L is contractible. For each root i its leaf link L_i has exactly two connected components: isolated own leaf and all other leaves, the latter connected by G-i. Thus adding v root cones to L yields pi_1=F_v. An original pair nonadjacent in G has an interior shortest-path vertex witnessing an allowable leaf triangle; an original edge uv has such a triangle iff some third vertex is equidistant from u,v. A nonwitnessed edge cannot lie in any triangle, hence contributes one free generator. All remaining root-pair edges admit cancelling leaf-triangle pairs; all later two-root/one-leaf and three-root triangle boundaries are null after identifying nonisolated link-component arrows. Higher faces do not affect pi_1. Abelianizing proves Z^{v+b(G)}, not merely a field-rank observation. Independent BFS and modular rank tests support finite cases but proof establishes all parameters.

value.rationale: The previously studied graph-corona general-position polynomial does not determine nonabelian topology. The theorem gives an all-parameter free-fundamental-group classification for a structurally natural large base class with a motivated edge equidistance defect, distinct nontrivial parity behavior on cycles, and the explicit v+|E(G)| rank for bipartite 2-connected base graphs. It provides a reusable topological method by contractible-leaf-cone decomposition and no additional arbitrary parameter restrictions.
